question: What are the minimum mounting heights for roadside signs in rural areas and in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian activity is likely?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Roadside signs in rural areas must be mounted with a minimum height of 5 feet, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement. In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely (or where the sign's view might be obstructed), the minimum height is 7 feet, measured to the top of the curb or, absent a curb, to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way. The same 5-foot/7-foot requirements apply to temporary traffic control signs in Part 6. Standards (mandatory): - "In rural areas, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 5 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - "In business, commercial, or residential areas where parking, bicyclist, or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, the minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the top of the curb, or in the absence of curb, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way, of signs installed at the side of the road shall be 7 feet (see Figure 2A-2)." - For temporary traffic control: "The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the pavement, of signs installed at the side of the road in rural areas shall be 5 feet (see Figure 6F-1)." - For temporary traffic control: "The minimum height, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the top of the curb, or in the absence of curb, measured vertically from the bottom of the sign to the elevation of the near edge of the traveled way, of signs installed at the side of the road in business, commercial, or residential areas where parking or pedestrian movements are likely to occur, or where the view of the sign might be obstructed, shall be 7 feet (see Figure 6F-1)." - Exceptions exist for specific signs: the MAINTAIN TOP SAFE SPEED sign follows the same 5-foot (rural) and 7-foot (urban) heights, while "Reference Location and Intermediate Reference Location signs shall have a minimum mounting height of 4 feet... and shall not be governed by the mounting height requirements prescribed in Section 2A.15." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-2 illustrates the 5 ft MIN. height for roadside signs in rural areas (panels A, B, D, E) and the 7 ft MIN. height in business, commercial, or residential areas (panel C), along with lateral offsets and secondary-sign heights. - [Image 2] Figure 6F-1 shows temporary traffic control sign installations with 5 ft MIN. in rural areas (panels A, B) and 7 ft MIN. in business, commercial, or residential areas with and without curb (panels C, D). - [Image 3] This page presents the Section 6F.02 text confirming the 7-foot height for signs in business, commercial, or residential areas and above sidewalks, together with Figure 6F-1 depicting the 5 ft and 7 ft minimums. - [Image 4] This full-page view of Figure 2A-2 shows the 5 ft MIN. rural mounting heights and the 7 ft MIN. height where parking or pedestrian movements are likely to occur. - [Image 5] This page contains the Section 2A.15 Standard text stating the 5-foot rural and 7-foot business/commercial/residential minimum heights, with reference to Figure 2A-2. - [Image 6] Figure 2M-3 shows recreational/cultural interest sign assemblies mounted at 5 ft MIN. in rural areas and 7 ft MIN. in business, commercial, or residential areas, consistent with the Section 2A.15 heights. Citations: - Section 2A.15 Standard §4 (p.58) - Section 2A.15 Standard §5 (p.58) - Section 6F.02 Standard §4 (p.790) - Section 6F.02 Standard §5 (p.790) - Section 2N.06 Standard §5 (p.534) - Section 2H.11 Standard §6 (p.466) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 6F-1 (p.790) - Page 831 - Page 92 - Page 99 - Page 566
gold_answer: The minimum is 5 feet in rural areas and 7 feet in business, commercial, or residential areas where such activity or obstruction is likely, measured as specified from the near pavement edge or curb.
